title: Network kindly, prove your work and plan your next 90 days

say: Network kindly, prove your work, and plan your next 90 days.
This is the video for module four of Personal Branding and Online Presence.
Networking online follows the same rules as networking at a wedding. Introduce yourself politely, show interest in the other person, offer value before you ask for anything, and follow up.

say: The most common mistake is a stranger getting a message like: Hello ma, please I need a job in your company. It asks for a big favour before any relationship exists.

panel.heading: Kemi connects without being pushy
left: Please I need a job, kindly help
A big favour from a stranger
right: Follows and reads for two weeks

say: For example, Kemi wants to move into customer experience at a fintech company. She follows a manager there and reads her posts for two weeks, then leaves one thoughtful comment from her own experience.
Her note names the post she enjoyed, her six years in bank customer service, and asks only to connect. A month later she asks for a 15-minute chat, and the manager says yes.

say: Not every friendly contact is genuine. Be careful with anyone who quickly moves to money or asks for an upfront processing fee for a job. Real employers do not charge applicants to be hired.

cards.d: Real employers do not charge applicants to be hired.
Meet new contacts in public or by video call first, and tell someone where you are going.
Never add people to your groups or broadcasts without asking. Give an easy way to leave.

say: And on your side, never add new contacts to your sales group or broadcast list without asking. After two polite follow-ups with no reply, move on graciously.

say: Now your proof. Open your Brand before album from module one, take matching after screenshots, and place each pair side by side. Remember Amaka, the Lagos cake baker. Before, her WhatsApp scored 1 out of 5.
After: a clear name and photo, a useful About line, a catalogue of 10 cakes with starting prices, plus greeting, away and quick replies.
After 6 weeks, her enquiry log showed 9 new customers. Her capstone page shows both screenshots, a list of 8 changes, and that real result.
Your work portfolio needs three to six strong, recent pieces. For each, say what the client needed, what you did and the result. Then prepare a short spoken pitch.
Halima says: I help small shop owners in Kano see their real profit each month.
Last quarter, one pharmacy client found it was losing money on two product lines and dropped them.
If you run a shop, I can do a free 20-minute review of your records.
Aim for about 75 words. Only claim results you directly caused or contributed to.
A brand stays strong with a simple routine and a plan with dates. For example, Blessing, the Benin City hairstylist, starts from her log: about 12 new WhatsApp enquiries a month, 3 from Instagram.
In days 1 to 30 she fixes gaps. Her target is 5 written client reviews, with permission, by day 30.
In days 31 to 60 she keeps posting and connects with 15 salon owners or managers on LinkedIn.
By day 90 she aims for 18 enquiries a month, at least 6 from Instagram. Become famous is not a target. A number you can count is.

panel.heading: Blessing's plan with dates
panel.rule: Keep three targets at most, and set them from your own numbers.

say: Your practice. Start five relationships with comments and personal notes. Build your before-and-after document. Choose three to six portfolio items with permissions saved. Record your 30-second pitch, and write your 90-day plan with dated targets.
Now continue with the lessons below.
